correctness.rationale: Exact partition-independent sum of Fourier segment response columns is zero, so rank≤N−1. On the uniform grid with N≥2m+1, ±1,...,±m are pairwise distinct mod N, yielding discrete orthogonality and exactly W_N=π diag(sinc²(jπ/N)I₂). Weighted least squares and sinc monotonicity give the exact energy and sharp π²/4 limit. Direct numeric integral/Gramian tests supplement, not replace, proof.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge statement-level comparison: bounded bang-bang minimum-time switching conditions (Berlin et al. 2022) do not imply unconstrained fixed-horizon sampled minimum-energy reachability. General robust small-mesh reachability/convergence theorems (Bourdin–Trélat) do not fix the exact minimal number 2m+1 or furnish explicit sinc energy spectrum. Other known sampled-oscillator resonance and Fourier projection results address different questions and do not imply the stated all-mode resource-and-energy theorem. Residual risks explicitly stated.

value.rationale: The claim solves a natural minimal sample-hold resource problem in a multi-mode single-input control family exactly, including a lower bound valid for arbitrary partition knots and a matching uniform design. Its sharp universal π²/4 bound controls worst-target extra minimum energy at the precise minimal hold budget, providing a nontrivial quantitative finite-design benchmark. The scope is physically motivated by common-actuator oscillators and is not a gratuitous numerical instance.
